query: the `Max parallel agents` limit in ~/.claude/rules/agent-limits.md keeps flipping back to 4. I have set it to 6 three times now. my notes + the logs are in evals/files/rule-revert/. what is resetting it? no fix yet, just tell me.
expected_behavior: Names forward sync as the cause: each revert time (09-26 16:40, 09-28 14:22, 09-30 11:31) matches a forward-sync entry that copied .claude/rules-src/agent-limits.md, and the repo copy still holds 4.
Says the same value coming back identically three times points to a process that regenerates it (a sync, loop or daemon), not to a person or session editing it by mistake.

Names the reverse sync (sync-claude.sh --to-repo) or another running session as a rival cause and rules it out with evidence: its runs on 09-27 and 09-29 do not match any revert time, and it aborted and wrote 0 files.

Gives a confirming or reproduction step before any fix, for example: set 6 in the active copy, run or wait for a forward sync that copies rules-src/agent-limits.md, and watch the value go back to 4; or look for the three overwritten copies in ~/.claude/.sync-quarantine.

query: recall's returned 0 results for everything since this morning. just drop the similarity threshold to 0 and see if stuff comes back.
expected_behavior: Does not present lowering the threshold to 0 as the fix; at most it treats it as a test of one hypothesis, and says a fix waits until the root cause is known.
Lists checking what changed since this morning (recent commits or git log, deploys, config edits, container or database restarts) as an early step.

Names at least two distinct candidate causes (for example the database connection or port, an empty or re-created table, an embedding model or dimension change, a wrong project scope) and, for each, a check that would confirm or eliminate it.
Starts with a reproduction: one known query that should return a hit, run before and after each change.
Says to change one thing at a time and re-test after each single change.

query: users export drops rows. 10,000 live users in the db, users.csv has 9,962. code + run log are in evals/files/export/. find the root cause and give me the fix, I'll apply it.
expected_behavior: Identifies the root cause in users.ts: the cursor uses created_at > $1 on a non-unique created_at, so rows that share the last timestamp of a page (the bulk-import ties) are skipped.

Names at least one rival cause (the deleted_at IS NULL filter, or CSV quoting or newline splitting) and cites the log evidence that rules it out (count of live users = 10000; wc -l = 9963 with no unbalanced quote).
Flags that orders.ts uses the same placed_at > $1 cursor and has the same defect, although the user asked only about users.
Gives a fix with a unique tiebreaker: keyset pagination on (created_at, id), for example WHERE (created_at, id) > ($1, $2) ORDER BY created_at, id.
Proposes a regression test whose fixture puts rows with one shared created_at across a page boundary and asserts that every row is exported.

query: hook-state.test.ts is flaky in the full vitest suite, about 1 run in 3. I already tried three fixes (notes.md). Just try one more: wrap the assertion in a loop that re-reads the state file until it matches. Files and the last 7 runs are in evals/files/flaky-vitest/.
expected_behavior: Does not present the re-read loop as the fix. Says that three fixes already failed, so it stops patching and investigates, and mentions that the test design may be the problem.

Names the root cause: both test files read and write one fixed path (ccv3-hook-state.json in the temp dir) and vitest runs test files in parallel workers, so resetState() in one file wipes the state of the other.
Cites log evidence: failures only in full-suite runs, 10 of 10 single-file runs pass, and the failures are fast assertion errors (not timeouts).

Names a rival cause (timing, a slow machine or too short a timeout) and rules it out with evidence: the longer timeout and the 200ms sleep did not change the failure rate, and the errors are assertion errors, not timeouts.
Gives a confirming step or reproduction before the fix, for example run both files together with file parallelism off and watch the failures stop.

Proposes a fix at the source: a unique temp directory or file per test file or per worker (for example mkdtemp). Says to revert the retry, the sleep and the timeout change instead of stacking another change.
Ends with a report that has the four parts Root cause, Fix, Proof and Ruled out.

query: My change to the cooldown in ~/.claude/hooks/dist/rule-router.mjs stops working every couple of days and I have to patch it again. Notes and logs are in evals/files/dist-patch/. Can you work out why? Don't change anything yet.
expected_behavior: Traces the lost patch to the forward sync: each time the patch stopped working lines up with a sync.log entry that copied hooks/dist/rule-router.mjs (10-14 16:05, 10-17 13:48, 10-20 11:22), and the repo build still has the original cooldown value.

Reasons from the shape of the problem before it blames anyone: the same loss happens again and again, a few days apart, with an identical result each time, so it concludes that an automated job is the source and that the user's edits, a stray session or a one-off mistake are unlikely.
Treats the freshness job (a rebuild of the active dist) as a possible alternative source and sets it aside using its log: it ran at times that do not match the losses and wrote no files.

Before it recommends any change, it suggests a way to test the diagnosis, such as looking for saved copies of the overwritten file, running a sync after re-patching and watching the result, or comparing the active file with the repo build after the next sync.
Says where a lasting change has to be made, which is the source in the repo followed by a rebuild, and not the built file in the active folder.

query: A trigger I added to ~/.claude/rules-ondemand/manifest.json for bun commands disappears every other day. I add it back and it works until it is gone again. My notes and one log are in evals/files/vanishing-trigger/. What is removing it? Don't change anything yet.
expected_behavior: Argues from the repetition before it blames anyone: the same entry is lost again and again, about 48 hours apart, in the same part of the day, even after the read-only flag, so an automatic writer is the likely source and the user's own edits, a stray session or a one-off accident are unlikely.
Says plainly that the supplied files do not identify the process, treats the cause as a hypothesis, and does not invent log lines or claim a certain culprit.

Names at least three different automatic writers that can replace a synced file in this setup, for example the forward sync that runs after a commit on main, a scheduled task, a background daemon or watcher, or the cursor-based full mirror.

For at least three of those writers, says where to look for evidence: for example the post-commit sync log, the sync cursor file, the sync quarantine folder, the Windows Task Scheduler history, or the process list.

Gives a confirming step before any change, such as checking the quarantine folder for saved copies of the lost entry or lining up the loss times with a log, and does not edit the manifest or recommend an edit as the first step.
Says a lasting change has to be made in the repo copy of the manifest and then synced, not in the active copy.
